title: Screw Feeder

introduction.definition: A screw feeder meters bulk solids with a rotating helical screw in a trough or tube under a hopper. The screw flights move material forward like a nut on a thread. Its flights, pitch or shaft diameter usually vary along the inlet so material is drawn evenly from the whole hopper outlet, not just the back.
applications: Metering powders and granules (cement, lime, flour, chemicals)
Withdrawing from bins and bag dump stations
introduction.summary: A screw feeder meters bulk solids with a rotating helical flight in a trough. Each turn moves a fixed volume, so feed rate is set by speed. A variable-pitch flight draws material evenly from the whole length of the inlet.

foundation: Support on steelwork or a concrete plinth designed for the hopper/bin load on the feeder plus impact and dynamic loads.
Isolate vibrating machines from the structure with their springs/rubber mounts — never weld or rigidly bolt the vibrating body to the structure.
alignment: Set the feeder at the designed slope and centre it under the hopper outlet; set skirt boards and the hopper gate to the design bed depth.
Align drive and driven shafts (laser or dial gauge) or set the exciter motors as the maker specifies.
piping: Chutes and skirts: allow a gap that widens in the direction of travel so material does not jam; fit dust seals and connect dust extraction where required.
Leave clear access for liner change and for the hopper shut-off gate.
commissioning: Run empty first: check direction, amplitude/speed, temperatures and noise.
Load gradually, check the material bed is even and the discharge rate matches the set-point; record motor current as a baseline.

routine.task: Check discharge rate, noise and seal leakage.

periodic.task: Check flight wear and coupling condition.

lubrication: End bearings and gearmotor: lubricate to schedule.

symptoms: Rate higher than expected, product flushes through
remedies: Use shorter pitch, longer choke section or rotary valve
Check hopper design; use larger screw/lump breaker

safety: Guard the inlet — screws can draw in hands and clothing. Lock out before opening covers.

video_tutorials.title: Screw Feeder — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Screw Feeder.
A screw feeder meters bulk solids with a rotating helical screw in a trough or tube under a hopper.
The screw flights move material forward like a nut on a thread.
Its flights, pitch or shaft diameter usually vary along the inlet so material is drawn evenly from the whole hopper outlet, not just the back.
Typical applications include metering powders and granules (cement, lime, flour, chemicals); feeding mixers, kilns and dryers; withdrawing from bins and bag dump stations.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: U-Trough with Discharge Spout, Screw: Flight on Pipe Shaft (pitch sets volume per turn).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Screw Feeder — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Screw Feeder.
Check discharge rate, noise and seal leakage.
Check flight wear and coupling condition.
Replace screw/hanger bearings and liners.
Watch for flooding of fluid powders: rate higher than expected, product flushes through. Common cause: aerated powder.
Watch for overload/jamming: high current. Common cause: lumps, compaction under hopper.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
